decisions.title: FabControlBook
decisions.targetAudience: Fab process-control, equipment, yield, and integration engineers.
decisions.overlapEvidence: YieldBook statistics/signatures/classification/commonality and TestBook DC/limits chapters cover foundations, not an FDC/APC control-loop course.
decisions.uniqueValue: Control plans, signal lineage, equipment/process monitoring, alarm quality, FDC/APC response, change control, false alarms, and evidence selection.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Write original control engineering material with labeled synthetic series; link to YieldBook and TestBook for foundations.
reusePlan: Reference-only by default; any adaptation requires exact path/SHA/license/notice/change records.

decisions.title: ThinFilmBook
decisions.targetAudience: Deposition, epitaxy, materials, and integration engineers.
decisions.overlapEvidence: ProcessBook deposition is a broad CVD/ALD/PVD/epitaxy survey; DopingBook adds thermal-budget/metrology context, not a full interface/growth-physics course.
decisions.uniqueValue: Deepen surface kinetics, nucleation, conformality, epitaxy, interfaces, stress, defects, and film/device consequences.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Create original models/figures and validate each quantitative claim against public sources; link to ProcessBook and ProcessIntegrationBook.
reusePlan: Reference-only unless particular licensed files are separately cleared.

decisions.title: ReliabilityEngineeringBook
decisions.targetAudience: Semiconductor device, process, product, and reliability engineers.
decisions.overlapEvidence: FailureBook covers mechanisms/localization/root cause; TCADBook selected high-field effects; TestBook burn-in; DeviceBook device foundations. They do not form a unified mechanism-to-lifetime/qualification sequence.
decisions.uniqueValue: Develop degradation physics, acceleration-model assumptions, censored lifetime data, uncertainty, qualification design, field-to-test limits, and technology context.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Author original examples; link to FailureBook for FA and DeviceBook/TCADBook for physics. Label synthetic or uncalibrated models.
reusePlan: Reference-only by default; record exact material and MIT notices before any code adaptation.

decisions.title: AlgebraBook
decisions.targetAudience: Secondary learners who need a systematic first algebra course.
decisions.overlapEvidence: MathBook is an applied collection with selected limits, linear algebra, complex numbers, probability, and optimization, not a first elementary algebra course. Linear algebra is a distinct subject.
decisions.uniqueValue: Teach expressions, equations, inequalities, functions, graphs, systems, polynomials, and modeling progressively.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Write an original course; keep elementary algebra distinct from linear and abstract algebra; link MathBook for later applications.
reusePlan: Reference-only by default; no text, figures, questions, or code reused without file-level clearance.
decisions.scopeBoundary: Elementary algebra is distinct from linear algebra and abstract algebra.

decisions.title: CalculusBook
decisions.targetAudience: Advanced secondary and university science/engineering learners.
decisions.overlapEvidence: MathBook covers limits, ODE, Fourier, optimization, and numerics as application chapters, not a systematic single/multivariable calculus course.
decisions.uniqueValue: Build a progression through limits, derivatives, integrals, series, multivariable/vector calculus, and explicit modeling assumptions.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Create original lessons/examples and checked visualization; refer to MathBook for applications and connections.
reusePlan: Reference-only by default; do not copy prose, figures, questions, or code.

decisions.title: EngineeringMathBook
decisions.targetAudience: Engineering students needing applied undergraduate mathematics.
decisions.overlapEvidence: MathBook already spans complex values, linear algebra, Fourier, ODEs, probability, optimization, and numerics; My Library separately plans books in most of those areas.
decisions.uniqueValue: A later bridge course might connect tools to engineering problems, but no bounded audience or exclusive outcomes currently distinguish it.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Defer and use MathBook plus the focused planned sequence. Reconsider only if a distinct capstone course is evidenced.
reusePlan: Use reference links only; do not scaffold/register until an updated review defines its unique purpose.
unresolvedQuestions: Would a cross-book capstone path serve this need better than another standalone textbook?

decisions.title: HeavyVehicleBook — Little Builders
decisions.targetAudience: Preschool children around 3–5 reading with a caregiver.
decisions.overlapEvidence: Upstream CarBook is adult automotive engineering: 22 chapters and 140 simulator files on engine, dynamics, braking, EV, and ADAS. No preschool construction-vehicle book was found in the 43-record catalog.
decisions.uniqueValue: A read-aloud story can weave in a few concepts such as colors, counting, shapes, size, vocabulary, and cause/effect.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Write original bilingual stories/art and skippable interactions; connect existing concept IDs; cite vehicle facts.
reusePlan: Do not adapt adult CarBook. The existing pilot prose has no reuse license; choose and document rights before publication.

decisions.title: CarBook — Little Explorers
decisions.targetAudience: Preschool children and caregivers; distinct from the adult engineering title.
decisions.overlapEvidence: Upstream CarBook (22 chapters, 140 simulator files) teaches automotive engineering, not preschool picture-book reading.
decisions.uniqueValue: A child-centered story can explore movement, color, counting, shape, comparison, and Korean/English vocabulary without claiming professional depth.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Create original story/art, clearly disambiguate title/cover/metadata, and link concepts to future study.
reusePlan: Companion only; reference the engineering book by link, without adapting its text, figures, code, or simulators.
decisions.disambiguation: Not the existing geniuskey/CarBook engineering textbook.

decisions.title: DinosaurBook — Little Explorers
decisions.targetAudience: Preschool and early-elementary children with an adult.
decisions.overlapEvidence: No dinosaur/paleontology title occurs in the 43-entry catalog. BodyBook covers human physiology, not dinosaurs, fossils, or prehistoric life.
decisions.uniqueValue: An original story could connect curiosity with fossil evidence, time, habitat, comparison, and scientific uncertainty, leading toward biology/Earth history.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Create original story/art and fact-check species and timelines against public science/museum sources.
reusePlan: No upstream text identified for reuse; cite facts and clear illustration rights before release.
unresolvedQuestions: Which public museum/science sources should ground the first story?

decisions.title: PMICBook v1.2 engineering candidate
decisions.targetAudience: Power-management IC, analog, device, and BCD process learners who need circuit-to-device-to-process reasoning.
decisions.overlapEvidence: PMICBook is a declared ProcessBook CC BY 4.0 adaptation and MIT software derivative. ProcessBook covers broad fabrication; inspected portions of DeviceBook, DopingBook, TCADBook, and AnalogBook cover adjacent device, dopant, numerical, and LDO fundamentals. Those bounded readings do not establish a complete public BCD nLDMOS process or calibrated PMIC device model.
decisions.uniqueValue: Integrate PMIC circuit requirements, BCD architecture alternatives, source-specific nLDMOS module orders, bounded device physics, bilingual process interactions, and explicit model and source limitations in one educational course.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Extend the credited ProcessBook-derived book with PMIC-specific bilingual analysis and independently checked teaching models. Preserve adaptation notices; use the separately inspected reference books for bounded context and links, without treating a current reference snapshot as a new adaptation baseline.
reusePlan: ProcessBook educational adaptations and Korean translations retain CC BY 4.0 attribution, source baseline 0bc4314d1e13c485a658e0cb1d4fd237b5fc8dff, and modification notices.
Retained or modified ProcessBook software retains the applicable MIT permission and warranty notice; map code lineage in PMICBook docs/UPSTREAM_ATTRIBUTION.md.
The five current indexed books below were read only at the listed paths and SHAs for reference context. No blanket reuse or whole-book clearance follows from this bounded inspection.
unresolvedQuestions: Native-speaker Korean scientific prose review remains open.
A comparable public passive-platform density table and calibrated LDMOS design data remain outside the candidate evidence.

decisions.title: RobotBook — Little Explorers
decisions.overlapEvidence: DigitalBook covers gates/state machines/HDL and timing; ComputerBook covers computing. Upstream backlog lists RobotBook only as an idea; neither is a preschool read-aloud book.
decisions.uniqueValue: An original story may explore movement, patterns, sequences, and helpful instructions without claiming robots have human feelings or making reading a coding quiz.
decisions.developmentStrategy: Create original prose/art with optional interactions; link to DigitalBook/ComputerBook for later study.
reusePlan: Reference advanced texts by link only; no code, diagram, quiz, or UI adaptation.
unresolvedQuestions: Which vocabulary is age-appropriate without turning the story into a programming lesson?
